head_commit.message:
CI: compare the neural-ES default-path oracle within 1e-9 off its recording platform

test_defaults_bit_identical_oracle compared SHA-256 hashes of predictions
recorded on macOS arm64 (scikit-learn 1.9.1). CI runs Linux x86_64 with the
lock's scikit-learn 1.9.0, so the hashes could never match and CI has failed
on every push since b04f49b. The test now keeps the exact hash check on the
recording platform and versions and, elsewhere, compares the stored values
(rtol 1e-9, atol 1e-12) while still requiring identical epoch counts and model
selection. Under the CI lock on Linux the largest difference is 5.6e-16.

Frozen rule 2026-10-06-shift-transfer and its tool: zero-shot transfer of the descriptor ladder to deeper circuits (S4, depth 3 to 6) and stronger noise (S2, L1 and L3 to L4)

The rule fixes, before any fit on shifted data, the shifts, the data, two

workflow_runs.display_title: Rename the package to QEMScore, and leave the on-disk formats alone

head_commit.message:
Rename the package to QEMScore, and leave the on-disk formats alone

QEM-Bench (Bao et al., ICML 2025) is a benchmark for the same task and is cited
by the paper this package supports, so the old name collided with a work the
paper itself discusses. Nothing had been released under it. PyPI returns 404 for
qem-bench and this repository was private, so there are no installed users, no
external links and no redirect burden, and the rename can be complete rather
than partial.

Three spellings, by role. The module and import path are qemscore, because PEP 8
wants module names in lower case. The console command and its entry point are
qemscore. The project name and the repository are QEMScore.

Seventeen strings of the form qem-bench-<name>-v<N> are deliberately unchanged.
They are on-disk format identifiers, and three of them sit behind hard
validation gates: campaign/analysis.py rejects a record or a report whose
schema_version differs from its constant, and reports/generate.py rejects a
manifest that is not qem-bench-report-manifest-v1. Renaming them would make this
code reject every artifact that already exists, including the published
campaign-archive-v1 release and the frozen evidence the paper's numbers trace to.
That is a breaking format change needing a version bump and a migration path.
They carry their own -vN discipline, so the guard is mechanical: a qem-bench
followed by a hyphen is a schema string and stays.

requirements/ci-py312.lock is unchanged for a related reason. A comment line in
it carried the old name, and rewriting that comment moved the file's SHA-256
from 20ce2461 to 0c4e1eee. That hash is a reproducibility contract recorded in
pyproject.toml, in the workflow, and in artifact manifests, so a cosmetic edit
inside the file costs a contract update in three places and buys nothing.
tools/verify_ci_lock.py caught it and passes again.

campaign-archive/SHA256SUMS.txt was never at risk. Its 67 entries carry no
repository name and no occurrence of the old name.

105 files changed with 432 insertions against 432 deletions, which is what a
pure rename should look like. 1049 tests pass and one xfails, unchanged from
before the rename.

workflow_runs.name: foundation-ci
workflow_runs.display_title: Decompose one improvement, and bind the result to the run that made it

head_commit.message:
Decompose one improvement, and bind the result to the run that made it

Plan review round 7 replaced the paper's primary hypothesis. The two-point
evolution-step contrast is now a declared secondary, and the primary is a
decomposition of a single improvement. With A the affine feature-only error, C
the nonlinear feature-only error and F the full nonlinear error, all measured on
identical rows with identical aggregation:

    T = A - F      K = A - C      D = C - F      T = K + D      S = K / T

The published question asks how much error rises when a feature is deleted, whose
denominator is the model's own error. This asks what fraction of the reported
improvement needed the observation at all, whose denominator is the whole
improvement. Both answers can be large and small at once, which is the point.

`qem_bench/stats/improvement_share.py` is new and takes an ordered ladder rather
than a fixed A, C and F, because a second half of the same estimand needs a
four-rung nested ladder and two estimators would duplicate the bootstrap, the
pairing and the denominator rule. The ladder itself is frozen in the campaign
layer, so no caller can reorder or substitute a rung; a reversed ladder is
undetectable from method names alone. Every rung, span and reference method
shares one circuit-index resample per family, and S is formed inside each draw
rather than as an average of per-row ratios. It is never clipped, no draw is
discarded, and a negative gap is a result.

Three artifacts were written from the specification by three authors. The
implementation, the 45 test functions, and an exact-rational oracle whose author
had read neither of the others and was barred from numpy, because the estimator
depends on numpy and a shared dependency is a shared failure mode. The oracle
battery compares 24 randomized scenarios on exact rationals. One qualification:
the test author changed the `from_cell_errors` input encoding to match the
implementation, so on that one encoding the agreement is one-directional.

Three review rounds followed, all three returning BLOCK.

Round 8 found that an independent contrast rejected only an identical circuit
order, so two disjoint pools carrying one stream seed drew the same index vectors
and published a contrast of exactly zero width while declaring the sides
independent. It also rejected reporting the imported cell fields rather than the
caller's, since cells carry equal weight and redefining one changes the estimand.

Round 9 found the boundary that matters most before any measurement. The share is
computed from a record's retained rows while its audit identity is only the
dataset hash it names. Dropping one observable moved the share from 0.50 to
0.9375 with no prediction changed and both reports still reading frozen and
audited. It also found the new share inheriting none of the rehearsal and audit
restrictions, and a contrast bound to circuit names rather than to the table that
produced the estimate.

Round 10 found the receipt gap the row check leaves. Copying another method's
saved prediction map into the C slot moves S across its whole range, 0 with A's
map and 1 with F's, while rows, dataset hash, code revision and selected
configurations all stay unchanged. That is what a stale export or an arm-key
mix-up produces, and it cannot be reconstructed after the fact. `fit` now writes
a receipt of the complete record linked to the verified pre-fit freeze, `analyze`
verifies it first, and a sealed fit cannot be overwritten. Two independent fits
of one setting produce the same record digest, so the receipt is an identity
rather than a run artifact.

Round 10 also found every one of the 24 decompositions stamped primary, including
both regimes, both training sizes and rehearsals, while the table export carried
no share rows at all. Manual extraction from a uniformly primary grid was the
natural way to reach the paper's result. The six committed keys now live in
`declared_design()`, roles are read from them, and the whole ordered grid exports
with placeholders for what is absent. Choosing those keys after a run would have
been unacceptable; the renderer can follow.

Publication eligibility travels with the share, and only ever negatively:
`dirty_code_not_publishable`, then rehearsal, unaudited, unverified. No positive
value exists anywhere, and a test asserts its absence even when the older
replication rule says `promote_three_of_three`. A record fitted from an
uncommitted tree names a revision nobody can check out again, so it outranks the
other three.

`freeze_campaign.py` recorded `estimator.py` as `stimator.py`: `.strip()` on
`git status --porcelain` ate the leading status column, and `line[3:]` then
dropped a character. It also now refuses a dirty tree outright.

The reporting rule is frozen before any number exists. All six primary
decompositions are reported together and no single scalar share is claimed. The
largest is not selected, the six are not averaged, and pooled gaps and totals are
not ratioed, because each is a different estimand and this estimator licenses
neither. A small share, a negative gap and a withheld share are reported as they
come.

What this does not establish. No campaign has run and every number in the paper
is still unmeasured. Round 10 assessed the thesis and found the controlled half
cannot carry a claim about error mitigation as a field: within a regime, family
and observable, the feature-only input determines the target-generating circuit,
since TFI varies two continuous physical dimensions and Heisenberg three and the
couplings reach the learner directly. Coupling polynomials on 32 rehearsal
circuits reach test MAE 0.0017 for TFI at degree three. The controlled half shows
that an evaluation can reward descriptor interpolation, not how often that
happens in published work. The strongest permitted conclusion is recorded in the
campaign plan as a ceiling rather than a target.

1049 tests pass on Windows x86_64 and on Linux aarch64 with identical counts.
Twenty-two mutations were run across the three rounds and every one is now
caught, including the two that survived round 8.

workflow_runs.display_title: Make the audit a precondition, and anchor the endpoint's scale

head_commit.message:
Make the audit a precondition, and anchor the endpoint's scale

Four review rounds against this change, two of which returned BLOCK.

`evaluate_campaign` would emit `design_frozen: true` and `promote_three_of_three`
with no audit having run. The requirement lived only in the campaign plan.
`_audit_bindings` now joins each setting to its audit, refuses an audit whose
dataset hash disagrees with the record, and stamps `unaudited_not_publishable`
when any setting is unaudited, failing, or missing its zero-noise replay. The
stamp runs before the rehearsal stamp, so a rehearsal still reads as a rehearsal.

A replay counts only when it names the bound roster artifact. Round 6 found the
first version accepted any truthy `zne_replay.checked`: the roster can be
regenerated from the same dataset, so agreeing dataset hashes prove nothing, and
a stale audit would authorize a roster it never saw.

The endpoint g = 1 - MAE_full / MAE_control is scale invariant, so a rise in the
control's error between regimes cannot be separated from a wider ideal-label
distribution. The evolution step moves both. `_label_spread` supplies the
missing units, formed inside each (noise family, severity, observable) cell about
that cell's median and macro-averaged over cells, which is the partition
`_macro_mae` uses.

`ARMS` declares two arms that move learner and control at once, so a divergence
between them cannot be attributed to either. `LEARNER_FIXED_CONTRAST` holds the
learner at `liao` and moves only the control. It reaches the endpoint tables and
stays out of `replication`, so it collects no promotion verdict and adds nothing
to the primary test family.

`analyze` reads `audit.json` when present and prints the three audit fields. A
missing audit is read rather than refused, because the rehearsal runs `analyze`
before any audit exists and the library already withholds the path.

The roster ledger printed `0undefined`: "undefined" is exactly as wide as the
ratio column, so it ran into the realized total.

Six mutations verified, each failing on its own assertion, each file restored
byte for byte. 792 tests pass with the four modules blocked by this machine's
mixed scipy install excluded.

head_commit.message:
feat: freeze the campaign manifest, and make the freeze checkable afterwards

The plan requires the design, the promotion rule, the audit rules and the code
revision to be fixed before any final score exists. A sentence saying so is not
checkable. `tools/freeze_campaign.py freeze` captures them into one dated file
along with the environment, the package versions that can move a histogram, and
every generated dataset's identity, then hashes its own body. `verify` re-reads
that file and names every field that has since moved, exiting non-zero when any
has, so a reader can tell whether the run that produced the numbers is the run
the freeze describes. It reports the whole drift list rather than raising on the
first difference, because after a campaign the useful output is all of it.

The driver gains `--regime`, so a maximum-size rehearsal can calibrate throughput
on one evolution-step regime rather than paying for both.

head_commit.message:
docs: withdraw a claimed impossibility the review disproved

Both audit modules said that an independent noise construction and an exact
histogram comparison could not both hold, because a second construction would
change the order in which the sampler consumes randomness. Round 5 of the plan
review built the L1 and L3 models separately and reproduced every sampled base
histogram exactly. The claim was wrong, and it was doing work: it dressed a gap
in coverage as a considered trade.

The audit shares the production noise model because that model has not been
reimplemented. The consequence is a fault class it passes, which round 5 also
executed: a sampler that requests the L1 model for an L3 row keeps every
parameter, identity, seed and recorded severity, and a replay through the same
wrong helper agrees with it. The frozen noise-model tests cover construction and
not which severity is requested. Both modules now say that.

head_commit.message:
feat: the campaign's primary endpoint, its record format, and an independent audit

The plan review found that the campaign specified an endpoint whose analysis
program did not exist. `circuit_blocked_bootstrap` computes a statistic or a
paired difference; it cannot form a ratio of two fitted predictors' errors and
then a difference between independent datasets. `stats/gain_contrast.py` is that
estimator: it resamples physical circuits inside a regime's pool so a circuit's
severities and observables travel together, shares each draw between the two
predictors, and recomputes both macro MAEs and their ratio inside every draw.

`campaign/` holds the frozen design as code, the assertions that run before any
fit, one self-contained record per setting, and an evaluation that reads only
those records. A record claims to belong to the frozen campaign only when its
seed, size, realized counts, resample count, confidence and diagnostic seeds are
all the frozen ones; anything else is a rehearsal, and no rehearsal reaches a
publication path whatever its numbers say.

`baselines/liao.py` takes `drop_features` on all three classes and deletes the
column inside the one feature-matrix helper every fit, validation and prediction
path already used, so the capacity-matched control is the same candidate family
by construction rather than by assertion.

`tools/audit_campaign.py` replays every pool instance's seeded parameter draw and
compares compiled features against every row, then replays a frozen sample's
histograms, labels and folded zero-noise executions. `tools/audit_protocol.py`
writes both Trotter protocols out from their specification and evolves the state
with plain arrays, importing nothing from the package, which is what catches a
label routine that agrees with itself everywhere.

Also fixes the report's cost axis: `set_xticks` widens a view rather than
replacing it, so panels whose points spanned different costs kept different
limits and their frontiers could not be compared by eye.

head_commit.message:
feat: split-aware reporting, an incremental-value gate, and a corrected release surface

Five review rounds on one staged change. What it adds:

- qem_bench/stats/incremental_value.py, the source-validation gate. A learned
  arm is credited with incremental value only when it beats both the
  feature-only and the noisy-only control by 1.05 in at least two continuous
  families, with each paired circuit-blocked interval strictly above zero. It
  is a claim gate rather than an equivalence test: failing it does not show
  that a method ignores its measurements, and the module says so.
- Split-aware metric cells. CELL_GROUPINGS carries split_id, so records from
  two evaluation settings can no longer merge under equal remaining fields.
  Legacy artifacts keep the old key and declare which one they use.
- Stratum separation in the report. Clifford controls no longer pool into the
  headline; they get their own section, and no Clifford cell enters a headline
  statistic. The example's ridge headline is 0.056577102850636725 over 18
  continuous cells, with the Clifford control at 0.03717038672274634 over 4.
- Two rendering defects that produced wrong output while exiting 0. The table
  was one unbreakable float and clipped 166.45pt of content at the full
  roster; it now emits one float per section with the header repeated. The
  split figure's legend grew one entry per method and split pair while the
  panel height did not, measuring 416.73 pixels against a 148.71-pixel panel;
  the figure now paginates one page per split, with a legend band whose height
  is computed from the roster before the panels are placed. Both fixes are
  pinned by tests checked against the defect rather than against a green suite.
- A caption that repeated one descriptor per run and made an ordinary 160-run
  campaign fail pdflatex with "Dimension too large" now names distinct presets.
- Family-conditioned shrinkage, a shuffle control that generalizes past ridge,
  and the release surface (README, CITATION.cff, pyproject.toml) corrected
  against what the code actually does.

825 to 827 tests, passing in both dependency-lock modes, with both frozen
dataset hashes regenerating byte-identical.

workflow_runs.name: foundation-ci
workflow_runs.display_title: fix: make derived results a function of the data, not of the platform

head_commit.message:
fix: make derived results a function of the data, not of the platform

The first CI run that ever completed failed three tests in test_examples.py that
pass locally, all reporting that a recomputed cell_records disagreed with the
stored one. validate_run_artifact recomputes derived results from stored
predictions and compared them with a bare inequality, so any cross-platform
float difference surfaced as an invalid artifact.

The first diagnosis was wrong and is worth recording, because the fix it implied
would have been harmful. It attributed the divergence to numpy reductions under
different BLAS builds and SIMD dispatch, and led to a six-decimal comparison
tolerance. A second environment built from the lock with PyPI wheels reproduced
the failure on Linux and refuted that account. Every measured reduction is
bit-identical across platforms: 3,960 reduction contexts and 768 quantile
contexts, zero differences, covering per-cell and headline metrics, pooled
diagnostics, macro quartiles, both grouping-sensitivity summaries, merged report
cells, mean ranks and the three 2,000-resample bootstrap intervals.

The entire divergence was three float leaves out of 14,764, all of them raw
per-item squared_error, computed as a scalar power. Platform pow is not
correctly rounded; the signed errors going into it were identical. The largest
difference was 6.94e-18. A six-decimal tolerance would have been about twelve
orders of magnitude wider than the defect it was absorbing, and would have
accepted a genuinely wrong recomputation as valid.

Squaring now multiplies instead. Multiplication is exact under IEEE 754, and the
formerly divergent input produces 0x1.cebbf533f6dd1p-5 on both platforms.

Two things are kept from the wrong-cause attempt because they are right for their
own reasons. Sums and means now use exactly-rounded summation, which turns an
observation that today's reductions happen to agree on today's inputs into a
property that holds by construction. Quantiles and the median now implement
Hyndman-Fan type 7 explicitly rather than taking a library default that can move
between versions.

With the pow source removed the measured divergence is zero, so artifact
validation keeps exact comparison rather than taking on a tolerance. It fails
closed on exact typed structure and exact finite binary64 bit patterns. The tests
that had been written to accept a tolerance were rewritten to require rejection
of a one-ULP float mutation, a float substituted for an integer, a boolean
substituted for an integer, identifier drift, extra structure, and nonfinite
floats.

Verified in the locked Linux PyPI-wheel image as well as under Miniforge on
Windows, because passing locally is what the previous state already did while CI
failed. All 14,764 committed derived float leaves now match exactly across the
two platforms. 692 passed and 1 xfailed in both lock modes, from 688.

Both frozen dataset hashes are unchanged; this touches the derived layer, not the
dataset layer. Published aggregates, run artifact identifiers and the example
bundle move, because they now bind to a specified algorithm instead of to
whichever kernel the host happened to dispatch.

workflow_runs.name: foundation-ci
workflow_runs.display_title: ci: pin a CPython patch that exists for the Windows runner

head_commit.message:
ci: pin a CPython patch that exists for the Windows runner

foundation-ci has run three times and failed three times. It has never passed.
Every failure is the same, and none of them is a code defect: the workflows pin
CPython 3.12.13, and actions/setup-python publishes that patch only for linux
and rhel. The Windows job dies in fifteen seconds at setup-python, before it
installs anything, and the missing .ci/frozen artifact and the failed gate are
downstream consequences. The Ubuntu crosscheck job has been passing throughout.

The lock file records that it was resolved against conda-forge python 3.12.13
for win-64, which is where the mismatch comes from: conda-forge publishes that
build for Windows and the GitHub runner tooling does not. 3.12.10 is published
for win32, linux and darwin, so it is pinned here instead. The lock file is not
touched, so its digest and the CI_LOCK_SHA256 constant are unchanged. All 3.12.x
share the cp312 ABI tag, so the pinned wheels install unchanged.

What this repairs is the ability to run the check, not the check's outcome, and
that distinction matters here. The frozen-streams job exists to install the
locked environment, regenerate both frozen item streams and assert their hashes.
Because it has never executed, those two hashes have so far been reproduced only
on one developer machine running 3.12.12. Every MATCH reported during the
preceding review rounds was a local result.

Passing both lock modes locally is also narrower than it sounds.
validate_environment_contract compares the recorded contract against the
CI_LOCK_SHA256 constant; it does not verify that the installed packages match
the lock. Proving that the locked environment reproduces the numbers is exactly
what this job does and what has been missing.

Whether 3.12.10 reproduces the two frozen hashes is therefore genuinely unknown
until this runs. That the patch level should not matter is an expectation, not
evidence: the hashes depend on the pinned library versions and the canonical
serialization rather than on CPython's patch number, and 3.12.12 reproduces them
locally. If the job now reports a mismatch, that is a real finding about the
reproducibility contract and must be investigated rather than accommodated by
loosening the assertion.

workflow_runs.name: foundation-ci
workflow_runs.display_title: fix: fold the recovered execution in the dependency-drift gate too

head_commit.message:
fix: fold the recovered execution in the dependency-drift gate too

The previous commit gave the production path the circuit that actually ran, and
that exposed a consumer which had been reading rows directly all along. The
dependency-drift snapshot parsed items.jsonl itself, rebuilt TFI from the rounded
row fields, and recorded folds of that approximation. While every path used the
rounded values the difference was invisible; once the runner moved to the
recovered execution, the gate was comparing a circuit that never ran.

Holding the snapshot's own fold seed fixed, every recorded frozen-preset fold
differed from the fold of the recovered circuit: 48 of 48 for t0-micro and 240 of
240 for t0-smoke. The workflow feeds those records to the drift comparison, so a
dependency change that altered the recovered binary64 execution while preserving
its 12-decimal serialization would have been reported as no structural drift. A
gate that can approve a dependency update without checking the physical programs
whose results get published is worse than no gate, because it is read as
evidence.

The snapshot now loads through the runner loader and folds through the same ZNE
rebuild the methods use. Its independent fold seed is kept; the defect was the
logical circuit going in, not the seed.

The unit that repaired the production path had enumerated circuit-rebuild
consumers by searching the qem_bench package, and this one lives in tools, so it
fell outside the search. This round enumerated from the repository root with an
AST inventory over every tracked Python file, covering tools, .github, tests,
examples and root documentation. That found no fourth defective consumer, and it
also separated the cases where reading rows directly is correct: the two dataset
generators are producers, the two canonical loaders are the things that establish
trust, and the viability probe samples fresh parameters rather than reading an
artifact.

688 passed and 1 xfailed in both lock modes, from 687. Both frozen dataset hashes
are unchanged and both raw item streams regenerate byte for byte. The example
bundle does not move, because the drift snapshot is not part of it.

workflow_runs.name: foundation-ci
workflow_runs.display_title: feat: CDR viability probe, reproducible example build, and honest sur…

head_commit.message:
feat: CDR viability probe, reproducible example build, and honest surfaces

**The CDR probe settles a gating decision.** Closest-angle replacement is not
viable across the shipped target grid, which the design notes suspected and
nobody had measured. The probe reports compiled non-Clifford counts, duplicate
rates, ideal-label spread, design rank and condition number per family and per
configuration, and recommends uniform Clifford replacement with
r = max(2, round(0.1 G)), execution-hash deduplication, and m = 70. It also
finds 18 QAOA target-observable rows where standard affine CDR is infeasible
because the design is symmetry or graph degenerate, which is a cost result
rather than a bug. Its JSON artifact reproduces bit-identically and now has an
integrity guard.

**The walking-skeleton example gets a build.** It had none: no script, no
documented command, and no test that ran the project validators over it. All
six shipped artifacts were silently invalid under the current code while the
whole suite passed, because the only test touching them compared a digest to
the manifest it was computed from. tools/regenerate_example.py rebuilds the
whole tree from one command, and tests/test_examples.py requires the six-file
inventory and validates every artifact, so the rot cannot recur unnoticed.

**PROTOCOL-TRACE was a table of nothing.** It declared an empty active set,
load_protocol_rules returned zero rules, the passing tests exercised temporary
fixtures, and no protocol marker existed anywhere in the repository. Six rules
now name six guards that genuinely enforce them. Two of those guards were
replaced this round because they overstated what they checked: one compared a
bootstrap estimate to a displayed mean without checking circuit blocking, and
one checked six prohibited names without enforcing family or version closure.

Authority is stated as absent rather than invented. An earlier revision pointed
every rule at a design document that lives in a separate private repository and
is not tracked here, which reads as a citation and resolves to nothing.

**README** describes what this batch ships and what it does not, including that
comparisons do not yet run at a matched circuit-evaluation budget and that the
Liao competitor is a restricted-feature ablation rather than a reproduction.

The protocol trace gate needed two repairs of its own. An integration pass had
replaced the assertion that each listed guard is actually collected with a
fallback that read the decorator out of the source text, which let a stale,
deselected, renamed, skipped or xfailed guard satisfy the trace. Listing a rule
whose guard does not run is worse than listing no rule, because it reports
enforcement that is not happening. The collection assertion is restored, the
session hook fails the run when a collected guard skips or xfails, and the
source scan survives as a separately named static catalog test. Both invocation
forms CI uses keep the runtime audit live.

Implementation references were also checked only as far as the file. A
reference naming a symbol that does not exist passed. Each one now must split
into exactly two non-empty components and resolve by AST to a top-level function
or class.

workflow_runs.name: foundation-ci
workflow_runs.display_title: feat: per-cell metrics, statistics, and the report layer

head_commit.message:
feat: per-cell metrics, statistics, and the report layer

qem_bench/runner/metrics.py computes per-cell metrics from run artifacts.
qem_bench/stats/ adds bootstrap confidence intervals, descriptive summaries,
paired inference, an out-of-distribution check, power analysis, and plots.
qem_bench/reports/ renders a table and a figure from a results manifest and
writes a report trace naming every input it read.

The run artifact identifier covers the result payload the reports consume,
not only the run configuration. An identifier that does not cover the numbers
downstream code reads gives no protection to the thing that actually moves.

The report trace records repository-relative paths only, and report
generation handles the shipped zero-measurement controls rather than dividing
by zero on them.

examples/report-walking-skeleton/ holds one end-to-end example: six run
artifacts, the results manifest, the trace, and the rendered table and figure.
Every file was regenerated from the current code and scanned byte-wise,
including inside the PDFs, for absolute paths, user names, and machine
identifiers.
